[Image #1] Build a 3D "Iron" tier badge for the BestSpent iOS app, as a RealityKit-ready USDZ, using the attached image as the look reference ("Forged Iron Crystal Medallion": a dark iron coin with a raised, faceted iron crystal in the center).

Work only in a NEW folder: ~/Downloads/badge_realitykit_iron/. Never modify anything in ~/Downloads/badge_realitykit_v3/, ~/Downloads/badge_realitykit_handoff/, or the app repo (~/Desktop/screen_time). Copy files you need; never edit the originals. Blender is at /Applications/Blender.app (run it headless: /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender --background).

START BY READING (these are the hard-won rules from the silver badge, which already ships in the app):
- ~/Downloads/badge_realitykit_v3/EXPORT_RULES.md (follow every rule)
- ~/Downloads/badge_realitykit_handoff/HANDOFF.md
- the scripts in ~/Downloads/badge_realitykit_v3/scripts/ (export_mobile.py, badge_mobile_rules.py, verify_floor_cut.py, compare_usd.py, reimport_check.py, render_proof.py, measure_smoothness.py, make_proof_sheets.py, compare_renders.py)
The silver master scene is ~/Downloads/badge_realitykit_handoff/scenes/silver_medallion_working_copy.blend; the shipped silver file is ~/Downloads/badge_realitykit_v3/mobile/silver_badge_mobile.usdz.

WHAT MUST BE IDENTICAL TO SILVER (the app depends on it):
1. The rim and the whole casing: reuse the silver casing, rim inner lip, inner edge, inner channel and inset disk GEOMETRY exactly (same dimensions, radius 3.015, back/front Z -0.345, same thickness, same profile, same bevels). Every tier's rim must be the same size and shape. Only their materials change.
2. Coordinates and framing: same scale, origin and orientation (USD Y up, 1 meter per unit, front faces +Z, no transforms), so the app's camera frames it exactly like silver.
3. Floor cut: cut every mesh at Y = -2.895 exactly as EXPORT_RULES rule 5 says (no cap).
4. Names: keep every object, mesh and material name identical to the silver v3 file (the app finds parts by name, e.g. the entity "Casing___smooth_rounded_outer_edge_mobile_geometry" and a material whose name starts with "Silver___circumferential_brushed_steel", whose brushed anisotropy the app restores at load because USD cannot carry it). Names are IDs here; the look changes, the names do not. If a name truly cannot be kept, list it in your report.
5. Budget: similar triangle count, texture sizes and file size to silver (about 3.5 MB USDZ).

WHAT CHANGES:
- The emblem: replace the silver spear with the iron crystal from the reference: an elongated, irregular, many-faceted crystal, slightly asymmetric, tilted as in the image, centered on the inset, about the same height, width and depth as the silver emblem so it sits the same way in the frame. Facets must be clean, flat planes with crisp edges.
- Materials: dark forged iron instead of silver. Rim and casing: a darker, slightly warm gray brushed iron with the same circumferential brushed direction. Emblem: lighter iron with distinct facet tones so the shape reads clearly. Inset: near-black charcoal like silver's. Keep metallic and roughness values in the same ranges as the silver materials so the app's lighting treats it the same.

SMOOTHNESS IS THE TOP RULE (the owner rejects any surface noise):
- Do NOT reproduce the reference's pitting, hammer marks, scratches, scuffs, crackle or mottling. Convey "iron" through color, tone, roughness and facet shape only. Every facet, the ring and the inset must look perfectly smooth on a phone: no grain, blotches, banding, streaks, seams or sparkling dots.
- No baked normal maps on any metal (rule 3). Facet shape lives in geometry and custom normals.
- Set each Bevel modifier's own bevel material so the rules script folds sub-pixel bevel strips into their facets (rules 1 and 2). Keep the gem edges clean: do NOT add widened bevel glints (the owner rejected that once; never propose it).
- The inset may keep a very subtle normal map only if baked at the strength it should show (rule 4); if in doubt, leave it flat.

PROCESS:
1. Build the iron master in a COPY of the silver master scene (silver casing geometry untouched, new emblem, new materials). Save it as scenes/iron_medallion_master.blend.
2. Export with the v3 pipeline on a copy (export_mobile.py with the floor cut at -2.895, then badge_mobile_rules.py). Output: mobile/iron_badge_mobile.usdz, plus scenes/iron_badge_mobile_reduced.blend and scenes/iron_badge_mobile.blend.
3. Check: usdchecker --arkit; reimport_check.py; verify_floor_cut.py; compare_usd.py against the silver v3 file (casing, rim and inset prims must match silver's geometry and bounds; only the emblem geometry and material values may differ; report every difference); render_proof.py, measure_smoothness.py, make_proof_sheets.py, compare_renders.py.
4. Look at your own proof renders zoomed in on every emblem facet, the rim and the inset. If you see any grain, blotch, streak, seam or sparkle, fix it at the source (model or material) and re-export. Do not hide it.

DELIVER in ~/Downloads/badge_realitykit_iron/:
- mobile/iron_badge_mobile.usdz (and its textures folder)
- scenes/ (master, reduced, final)
- proof/: a front render and a 3/4 render with the app's lighting, a side-by-side with the silver badge at the same scale (rims must match exactly), zoomed smoothness crops, and the measure_smoothness numbers
- REPORT.md: what you built, every check's output, the triangle count and file size vs silver, the material table (name, color, metallic, roughness), any name you could not keep, and anything you were unsure about.
Do not touch the app; integration into the app happens separately.

The iron badge loads and renders correctly in the app, but needs two look fixes. Keep every rule from before (silver casing geometry, all names, floor cut, no normal maps, perfectly smooth surfaces, no pitting or scratches).

1. Rim: the outer edge material (Outer_edge___smooth_satin_silver_Mobile_Casing, now 0.105) is so dark it reads as a black outline around the coin. Bring it close to the brushed face so the rim reads as one continuous iron band, and raise the whole rim (brushed face and outer edge) to about 0.22-0.26 linear so it stays darker and warmer than silver but clearly metallic, like the reference's rim. Keep the back/gunmetal dark.
2. Crystal: it reads as a plain low-poly rock (98 triangles, most of the lower half near black). Rebuild it closer to the reference: a clear center ridge running top to bottom, about 12-16 broad flat planes arranged around that ridge (left and right shoulders, a lower point), so light catches several faces at once. Raise the facet tones (main facets about 0.45-0.5 linear, shaded facets about 0.25-0.3) so no large face goes black under the app lights. Facets stay perfectly flat and crisp; no widened bevel glints.

Then rerun the full export and every check, and update proof/silver_vs_iron_same_scale.png and REPORT.md. Put the result in the same folder, replacing the previous iron files, and keep a copy of the previous version in a subfolder named previous/.

Rim is fixed, keep it exactly as is. One problem left: the crystal now reads as a busy, crumpled low-poly patchwork of small triangles in different shades, with no clear center ridge. Fix:
1. Every visible plane must be truly flat: all triangles of one plane share one normal, so each plane renders as a single even tone. Check this numerically and report the max normal difference within each plane (should be 0).
2. Fewer, larger planes: about 10-14 in total, arranged around one clear vertical center ridge from the top point to the bottom point, with a left side and a right side like the silver spear (left planes lit, right planes shaded), but keeping the iron crystal's irregular, slightly asymmetric outline from the reference.
3. No tiny slivers or small triangles visible from the front; every plane should be clearly readable at phone size.
Keep all other rules (silver casing, names, floor cut, no normal maps, smooth, crisp edges, no widened glints). Also raise the back/gunmetal material from 0.004 back to about 0.05 linear. Rerun the export and all checks, update the silver comparison proof and REPORT.md, and keep the current version in previous/v2/.

Finish the Iron badge yourself: iterate until it passes every check below, testing it inside the real app each time. Max 8 iterations; if it still fails after 8, stop and report the best one and what blocks it.

KEEP every earlier rule: silver casing geometry and the current rim/casing materials untouched (they are approved), all object/mesh/material names unchanged, floor cut at -2.895, no normal maps, perfectly smooth (no pitting, scratches, grain), crisp edges, no widened bevel glints.

STARTING FIXES (from the in-app test of v3, see ~/Desktop/badges/badge_realitykit_iron/app_reference/):
- The top-left plane mirrors the key light at rest and renders pure white with a glow halo (iron_v3_blown_top_facet.png). Tilt it (and any plane that does the same) so no plane mirrors a light at rest; lower the main facet color toward 0.40 linear if needed.
- Neighboring planes on the same side are too similar, so the lower half reads as one gray side and one dark side. Make neighbors differ by about 8-12 degrees, stepping from light near the ridge to darker at the outline on the shaded side, like the silver spear.
- No horizontal band or roof shape at the top: the top planes meet the ridge and slope down like silver's.
Change one or two things per iteration so you know what helped.

HOW TO TEST IN THE APP (the ground truth; Blender proofs alone are not enough). Repo: /Users/antonioperedo/Desktop/screen_time. You may temporarily replace ONE file and must always put it back:
  cd /Users/antonioperedo/Desktop/screen_time
  F=ScreenTime/SupportingFiles/Assets.xcassets/TestBadge3DModel.dataset/silver_badge_mobile.usdz
  git status --porcelain -- "$F"      # must print nothing; if it prints anything, stop and ask
  cp <candidate.usdz> "$F"            # same filename on purpose
  tools/sim/app build
  tools/sim/app launch; sleep 15
  # The first launch after install always shows the flat fallback badge (shader compile). Relaunch twice:
  for i in 1 2; do xcrun simctl terminate 69A29DD2-C91E-487A-81B9-3B146DF8F07B com.antonioperedo.screentime.uidev; sleep 1; xcrun simctl launch 69A29DD2-C91E-487A-81B9-3B146DF8F07B com.antonioperedo.screentime.uidev; sleep 15; done
  tools/sim/shot <iterations/NN/app_rest.png>
  git checkout -- "$F"                # ALWAYS restore, also after any failure
  git status --porcelain -- "$F"      # must print nothing
Never edit any other repo file, never commit, never switch branches. Measure with:
  /usr/local/bin/python3 ~/Desktop/badges/badge_realitykit_iron/app_reference/measure_app_shot.py <app_rest.png>

PASS CRITERIA (all in the same iteration):
1. App: loaded_3d=True. (If False, relaunch once more and wait 20 s; if still False, the file is broken: find out why.)
2. App: emblem_clip <= 800 (silver is 796; v3 was 4934).
3. App: rim_top within 147 +/- 5 (rim unchanged).
4. App, judged by eye next to app_reference/app_silver_rest.png and the original reference image: no plane pure white, no glow halo; one clear center ridge; left planes lit, right planes shaded, each plane a visibly different tone; no roof/band at the top; irregular, slightly asymmetric outline like the reference; nothing looks like crumpled foil. Silver's polish level is the bar.
5. Blender, app point-light rig, front at rest, with a per-plane ID mask: neighboring planes differ by at least 10 display levels; no plane brighter than silver's brightest emblem facet in the same render; no plane mean below 15.
6. Smoothness: measure_smoothness facet mean and edge excess mean no worse than silver's (0.92 / 61.5 stage, 1.00 / 64.6 harsh).
7. Every plane truly flat (max normal difference within a plane 0), and compare_usd vs v3 shows only emblem geometry and the two emblem materials changed. usdchecker --arkit, reimport_check.py, verify_floor_cut.py pass.

RECORD each iteration in ~/Desktop/badges/badge_realitykit_iron/iterations/NN/: the usdz, app_rest.png, the measure output, the Blender metrics, and 2-3 lines on what you changed and the result.

DELIVER: copy the passing iteration to mobile/iron_badge_mobile.usdz (move the current v3 to previous/v3/ first), add a final side-by-side of app_silver_rest.png and the passing app_rest.png, and update REPORT.md with a table of every iteration's numbers. Confirm at the end that git status in the repo shows nothing from you.

Iron v5 is approved; keep everything. One optional tweak: it reads slightly matte next to silver. Let one or two upper-left planes catch a controlled highlight so the crystal has a little shine: in the app test, emblem_clip between 150 and 500 (silver is 796, so iron stays a bit duller), with no glow halo past the crystal's edge and every other pass criterion still met. Same in-app test and restore procedure as before. Keep v5 in previous/v5/.

Promote candidate 08 as the final Iron badge. Its two misses (624 clipped pixels vs the 500 cap, 9.987 vs 10 tone gap) were arbitrary limits; it stays under silver's 796 and shows no halo. Copy iterations/08's usdz to mobile/iron_badge_mobile.usdz (v5 stays in previous/v5/), update the final silver comparison and REPORT.md, and confirm git status in the app repo is empty.

Read ~/Desktop/badges/AGENTS.md again first; it changed today. Section 2B covers shapes. Section 4 rule 8: the app no longer uses the soft ring light at all; every badge, coins and shapes, is lit by the original studio light only. Do not add the ring anywhere.

Task: make Silver 2 (~/Desktop/badges/badge_variants2_20261008/silver2/, current final 24) look as close as the app allows to the reference, source/silver_reference.png: polished silver, not grey plastic.

Why it looked flat: a soft ring light the app used until today lit every direction the star faces and leaves reflect, so nothing dark showed in them. It is gone now. Every app number and screenshot you have for Silver 2 is stale. Start by taking a new app baseline of final 24 under the current light (same test steps as before, three launches, 15 s waits).

What the reference does that the app still does not, in order of impact. Change one or two things per numbered candidate.

1. A gradient across every face. Each flat star face in the reference fades smoothly from brighter to darker, like polished metal reflecting a big soft light. In the app each face is one flat tone. Put one straight, smooth ramp per star plane in the color map, brighter toward the upper left key light and darker away from it, about 20 to 35 percent brightness change across the plane, each plane with its own direction so neighbors stay distinct. Add a gentle ramp along each leaf too. ONE ramp per plane: no valleys, bowls or bands inside a plane (finishes 20 to 22 showed those read as folds in the app). No banding: build the ramps at high bit depth so the 8 bit map keeps enough levels across each plane.
2. Warm and cool. Lit faces slightly warm (cream), shaded faces slightly cool (blue grey), like the reference. Subtle.
3. Range. Brighter faces toward the key and at the tips, darker shaded faces, never dead black. Under the current light the darkest star faces are already very dark, so lift them a little. For Silver 2 the owner allows the whole badge white count (screenshot box x 360 to 845, y 340 to 812) up to 2000 instead of 1249, as long as no glow halo shows past the edge of the star or any leaf; prove it with zooms. Every plane mean at least 30, neighboring star planes at least 25 levels apart.
4. Optional outline border, delivered as a separate candidate so the owner can choose by eye: a thin rounded border along the star's OUTER outline only, catching a thin bright line like the reference. Nothing along the inner ridges (wide ridge glints stay banned, rule 4.2). Deliver your best finish both without and with the border.
5. Leaves: keep their curved shine, add the ramps and the tint, and bright leaf edges like the reference where the geometry allows.

Keep: geometry (except the optional border), names, the shape frame (section 2B), no normal maps, no grain, mottling, stripes, folds or sparkle (rule 4.1), brushing no stronger than final 24. Gentle ramps are fine even though they do not move with the light during the one second entrance spin; never paint a sharp spot highlight.

Testing: the owner's Home preview stays installed. Silver 2 lives in ScreenTime/SupportingFiles/Assets.xcassets/Badge3DModelSilver.dataset/silver_badge_mobile.usdz. Test a candidate by replacing only that file and put final 24 back after every test. Never edit app code. Install the owner's pick only after they choose; until then leave final 24 installed.

Deliver: numbered candidates (usdz, app screenshot, measurements, two lines on what changed), a side by side of the reference and the app at the same size for your best candidate without and with the border, and an updated REPORT.md. Iron 2: only take one new app screenshot under the current light with the usual numbers; do not change it.

Keep going until the star reads as polished silver next to the reference at Home size with every rule passing, or 10 candidates, then report the closest one and exactly what still differs and why.
